entries.title: Titus 1:1
segments: From Paul, a servant of God, and an Apostle of Jesus Christ, charged to strengthen the faith of God's Chosen People, and their knowledge of that Truth which makes for godliness, .

entries.title: Titus 1:2
segments: and is based on the hope of Immortal Life, which God, who never lies, promised before the ages began,

entries.title: Titus 1:3
segments: and has revealed at his own time in his Message, with the proclamation of which I was entrusted by the command of God our Savior.

entries.title: Titus 1:4
segments: To Titus, my true Child in our one Faith: May God, the Father, and Christ Jesus, our Savior, bless you and give you peace.

entries.title: Titus 1:5
segments: My reason for leaving you in Crete was that you might put in order what had been left unsettled, and appoint Officers of the Church in the various towns, as I myself directed you.

entries.title: Titus 1:6
segments: They are to be men of irreproachable character, who are faithful husbands, whose children are Christians and have never been charged with dissolute conduct or have been unruly.

entries.title: Titus 1:7
segments: For a Presiding-Officer, as God's steward, ought to be a man of irreproachable character; not self-willed or quick-tempered, nor addicted to drink or to brawling or to questionable money-making.

entries.title: Titus 1:8
segments: On the contrary, he should be hospitable, eager for the right discreet, upright, a man of holy life and capable of self-restraint,

entries.title: Titus 1:9
segments: who holds doctrine that can be relied on as being in accordance with the accepted Teaching; so that he may be able to encourage others by sound teaching, as well as to refute our opponents.

entries.title: Titus 1:10
segments: There are, indeed, many unruly persons--great talkers who deceive themselves, principally converts from Judaism,

entries.title: Titus 1:11
segments: whose mouths ought to be stopped; for they upset whole households by teaching what they ought not to teach, merely to make questionable gains.

entries.title: Titus 1:12
segments: It was a Cretan--one of their own teachers--who said: 'Cretans are always liars, base brutes, and gluttonous idlers'; and his statement is true.

entries.title: Titus 1:13
segments: Therefore rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the Faith,

entries.title: Titus 1:14
segments: and may pay no attention to Jewish legends, or to the directions of those who turn their backs upon the Truth.

entries.title: Titus 1:15
segments: Everything is pure to the pure-minded, but to those whose minds are polluted and who are unbelievers nothing is pure. Their minds and consciences are alike polluted.

entries.title: Titus 1:16
segments: They profess to know God, but by their actions they disown him. They are degraded and self-willed; and, as far as anything good is concerned, they are utterly worthless.
